name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,743

clue.text: Andrew possibly has part to play with various nations

indicators.note: various means assorted or of differing kinds, so the letters come out in a differing arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Andrew has a role to play among many different countries.
explanation.walkthrough: The mix is PART plus NATIONS rearranged. 'Possibly' marks Andrew as just one example: St Andrew is the patron saint of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Andrew is one example of a holy protector adopted by a country, namely Scotland.

clue.text: Came before or went after

blocks.note: first meaning: existed earlier than
second meaning: hunted as prey, like a predator

explanation.walkthrough: The clue looks like a contrast of before and after in time, but 'went after' means chased, the verb behind the noun predator.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both existed earlier than something and, in zoology, hunted other animals for food.

clue.text: Change nails at first in defective rafters

indicators.note: what comes at first is the opening letter, so only the initial is kept
something defective is faulty or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the first letter of nails
taken as written

explanation.surface: A builder advises swapping in new nails on some faulty roof timbers.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes in among RAFTERS and the whole lot is rearranged; 'in' simply adds the letter to the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: To transfer is to move something from one place or owner to another, a synonym for change.

clue.text: Veteran squaddie stripped bare

indicators.note: stripping something bare removes its outer covering, so the outside letters go

blocks.note: a squaddie is British slang for a private soldier

explanation.surface: An old army private is left with nothing on.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the first and last letters of SOLDIER. A squaddie is British army slang for a low-ranking soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldie is an informal term for an older person, one who has been around for a long time, like a veteran.

clue.text: Correct garment in bed?  On the contrary

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it
the phrase swaps the roles just described, so the outer and inner parts trade places

blocks.note: a suit is a garment
taken as written

explanation.surface: Should you put your clothes on in bed? No, the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the garment goes inside the bed; 'On the contrary' flips the roles, so the garment does the holding.
explanation.definitionFit: To subedit is to check and fix copy for publication, so it means to correct written text.

clue.text: Immigrant's right to get money up front

indicators.note: being up front means coming first, so one piece goes before the other

blocks.note: income is money earned
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A newcomer to the country claims the right to be paid in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up front' puts INCOME above R. The 's is read as 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An incomer is someone who has recently arrived to live in a place, which is what an immigrant does.

clue.text: Move entrance

blocks.note: first meaning: carry from one place to another
second meaning: the verb en-TRANCE, to delight or enrapture

explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' looks like a noun for a doorway, but it is the verb meaning to fill with delight, stressed on the second syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to convey goods or people somewhere and to carry someone away with strong emotion.

clue.text: Every well-known retailer is abandoning shopping arcades

indicators.note: something abandoning a place leaves it, so those letters go out of the word

blocks.note: M&S, Marks & Spencer, a British high-street chain
malls are shopping arcades

explanation.surface: Every big-name store is pulling out of the shopping centres.
explanation.walkthrough: Take M and S out of MALLS. Marks & Spencer, written M&S, is a famous British department store chain.
explanation.definitionFit: All and every are both determiners covering the whole of a group without exception.

clue.text: Menu finale is in the oven

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it

blocks.note: an Aga is a British brand of range cooker
the finale is the end

explanation.surface: The dessert to finish the meal is still baking.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a large cast-iron range cooker found in many British country kitchens, which is why 'the oven' can name one.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu can be any list of items to deal with, such as the business points listed for a meeting.

clue.text: Former heritage organisation is inactive

blocks.note: late means former, as in the late president
NT is the National Trust, a British charity that looks after historic houses

explanation.surface: A defunct conservation body is now doing nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust, abbreviated NT, is the British charity that preserves historic buildings and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something latent exists but is dormant, not yet showing or developed, so it is inactive.

clue.text: South African native found in European country

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
a land is a country

explanation.surface: A person born in South Africa turns up living in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Native' suggests a person, but it is an animal native to Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large antelope whose natural home is the grassland of southern Africa.

clue.text: Reach out having no money for accommodation here in Romania

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged
accommodation houses a guest, so one piece lodges inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
to be bust is to be broke, with no money

explanation.surface: A penniless traveller asks for help with lodging in Romania.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reach out' reads as a plea for help, but 'out' mixes the letters; the result is housed in BUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucharest is the capital city of Romania, so it is a place located there.

clue.text: Husband leaves pet with mother in city

indicators.note: whoever leaves goes away, so that letter departs from the word

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
a hamster is a pet
a dam is an animal mother

explanation.surface: A husband walks out, leaving the pet with its mother in town.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove H from HAMSTER, then add DAM, the word for the mother of an animal such as a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Amsterdam is the capital of the Netherlands, one example of a large urban settlement.

clue.text: South of France abutting a northern country

indicators.note: to abut is to border directly, so the pieces sit side by side

blocks.note: sud is French for south
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: The south of France borders a country to the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South of France' looks like the Riviera, but it means the French word for south.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudan is a nation in north-east Africa, an example of a sovereign state.

clue.text: Handsome dumbo good for pub

indicators.note: one thing given for another is exchanged for it, so a letter swap takes place

blocks.note: Dumbo is the flying elephant of the Disney film
G is the abbreviation for good
PH is the abbreviation for public house on maps

explanation.surface: A good-looking fool is fine for a night at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dumbo' looks like an insult, but it is the Disney elephant. 'Pub' as two letters comes from the abbreviation for public house on British maps.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsome can describe something stylish and graceful in appearance, which is what elegant means.

clue.text: Astonished by cockney's articulated equine trailer

indicators.note: a cockney drops the H at the start of words, so the sound is what matters
articulated means spoken, so it is the pronunciation that counts

blocks.note: a horse truck with the H dropped, as a Londoner would say it

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed by a London driver's jointed horsebox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articulated' teases the articulated lorry, but here it means pronounced. Cockney is the accent of working-class East London, known for dropping H.
explanation.definitionFit: To be astonished is to be struck with wonder, filled with sudden amazement and awe.

clue.text: Space to dock, but turned and ...

indicators.note: something turned faces the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: to moor a boat is to dock it

explanation.surface: There was room to dock the boat, but it swung around and headed off.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this clue into 18 across, which continues the boating story.
explanation.definitionFit: Room means available space, as in enough room to park.

clue.text: Prospect of finding gold in Central American country

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: Panama is in Central America
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A prospector weighs the chance of striking gold in Panama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prospect' reads as a chance of success, but here it is a view. OR is gold in heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is an extensive view of a landscape, which is what a panorama is.

clue.text: Denys worried about memory and chronic fatigue?

indicators.note: worried means fretted or troubled, so the letters are disturbed
to be about something is to surround it

blocks.note: taken as written
ROM is read-only memory in computing

explanation.surface: Denys is anxious about his forgetfulness and constant tiredness.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: chronic fatigue syndrome is one named condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Chronic fatigue syndrome is a medical condition, so the question mark signals one instance of the wider category.

clue.text: ... went back to sea

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: peed, a slangy way of saying went to the toilet

explanation.surface: Continuing 15 across: the boat turned and headed back out to sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went' looks like travelled, but it is the euphemism for relieving oneself. The deep is a poetic name for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The deep is a literary name for the ocean, from the depth of open water.

clue.text: Bribe with hand cream?

blocks.note: first meaning: slang for a bribe, money that greases the palm
second meaning, cryptic: an oil for the inside of the hand

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading: literally a lubricant for the palm of the hand, not the tropical vegetable oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Greasing someone's palm means bribing them, so the oil used is the bribe itself.

clue.text: Insurance advisor surely right to replace students

indicators.note: to replace something is to take its place, so one piece swaps for another

blocks.note: actually and surely both affirm, as in really
R is the abbreviation for right
L is a learner, so two of them are students

explanation.surface: An insurance expert is certainly the right person to replace the trainees.
explanation.walkthrough: R replaces LL in ACTUALLY. L is a learner from the L-plates on British learner drivers' cars.
explanation.definitionFit: An actuary calculates risks and premiums for insurance companies, a professional who advises on them.

clue.text: Examine any sale that's suspect

indicators.note: something suspect is dodgy and not as it should be, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Investigate any sale that looks dodgy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a fraud investigator's instruction; the two words are the letters to mix.
explanation.definitionFit: To analyse is to study something closely in detail, which is to examine it.

clue.text: Spot for refills

blocks.note: surface reading: a good place to get your glass filled again
setter's reading: the first word of the answer, written upwards in a down light, spells this word, and the second word says so

explanation.surface: A place to go for more drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is its own instruction: in a down entry, write its first word going up and you read the clue's first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Refills and tops up both mean fills a glass or tank again to the brim.

clue.text: Times coverage of King is dull

indicators.note: coverage wraps around its subject, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: times as in multiplication, three by four
Lear is Shakespeare's king

explanation.surface: The Times newspaper's reporting on the monarch is boring.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic 'Times' dresses the word as the newspaper, but it is the multiplying 'by'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleary describes eyes or sight that are dim and blurred, so lacking sharpness, hence dull.

clue.text: Ordinary week allowed junior member of parliament to emerge

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for ordinary
W is the abbreviation for week
let means allowed

explanation.surface: An unremarkable week let a new backbench MP come to the fore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parliament' is not Westminster: a parliament is the collective noun for a group of owls.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of owls is called a parliament, so a young owl is a junior one of its members.

clue.text: Lee sold sound property agreement

indicators.note: sound points to how words are heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: said quickly, the name and the verb run together

explanation.surface: Lee sold a structurally solid property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective praising the property; it is the signal to listen.
explanation.definitionFit: A leasehold is a contract under which property is held for a fixed term of years, a type of tenure.

clue.text: A bender - wobble back half-heartedly

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the letters run backwards
doing something with half a heart loses half of the middle, so one central letter goes

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A drinking binge leaves someone staggering home unsteadily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bender' looks like a drinking spree, but it is literally something that bends. The reversed word has BB at its heart, and one B is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: The elbow is the hinge joint that lets the arm flex, so it is something that bends.

clue.text: Legal standing cut short by Conservative

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: status is standing or rank
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Conservative government curtails someone's rights in law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legal standing' looks like one phrase, but the definition is just 'Legal'. Tory is the everyday name for a British Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Statutory means required or permitted by statute, laws passed by a parliament, hence legal.

clue.text: Head over to see comic

blocks.note: bean is slang for the head
O is the abbreviation for an over in cricket

explanation.surface: Go across to watch a comedian perform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comic' looks like a comedian, but it is a comic book: The Beano is a long-running British children's comic.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beano is a weekly British children's publication of strip cartoons, featuring Dennis the Menace.

clue.text: Recompense fifty walking out of theatre production

indicators.note: whoever walks out of a place leaves it, so that letter departs from the word

blocks.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
a play is a theatre production

explanation.surface: Audience members demand refunds after fifty of them storm out of a show.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove L, the Roman fifty, from PLAY.
explanation.definitionFit: To recompense is to compensate someone for work or loss, which is to pay them.

clue.text: Marine predator creates warlike hell

indicators.note: to create is to make something new, so the letters are built into a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sea hunter causes violent carnage.
explanation.walkthrough: The orca's fearsome reputation makes the surface read as a nature documentary.
explanation.definitionFit: The orca is an ocean-dwelling hunter that preys on seals, fish and even other whales.
